claim: The Olympic Museum is open Tuesday to Sunday 09:00–18:00, closed Mondays plus 24/25/31 December and 1 January, with last admission at 17:00.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday from 09:00 to 18:00 (9 AM to 6 PM), and closed on Mondays. The museum is closed on December 24, 25, 31 and January 1. Last admission at the museum is 5 p.m.

claim: Olympic Museum admission is CHF 20 full, CHF 14 reduced (seniors/students/disabled), free for children up to 15 with an accompanying adult.
quote: Full price (ages 16+): 20 CHF — Seniors, students, disabled visitors: 14 CHF — Children (up to 15 years): Free with accompanying adult

claim: Plateforme 10's three museums (MCBA, mudac, Photo Elysée) open 10:00–18:00; a combined 3-museum ticket is CHF 25 full / CHF 19 reduced, or CHF 15 for a single museum.
quote: Open from 10:00 to 18:00 ... Full price CHF 25.–, reduced price CHF 19.– ... I only want to visit this museum CHF 15.–

claim: Plateforme 10 is a 25,000 m² arts district by Lausanne station uniting MCBA (fine arts), Photo Elysée (photography) and mudac (contemporary design).
quote: Plateforme 10 is a 25,000 m² arts district in the heart of Lausanne, formed by the merger of the Musée Cantonal des Beaux-Arts (MCBA), Photo Elysée, and mudac

claim: Collection de l'Art Brut is open Tuesday–Sunday 11:00–18:00; admission is CHF 12 adult / CHF 6 reduced, free for under-18s and free for everyone on the first Saturday of each month.
quote: From Tuesday to Sunday: 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. ... Adult: CHF 12.– ... Reduced rate (AVS/AI, Caritas Culture Card, groups of 6 or more): CHF 6.– ... Free admission for everyone on the first Saturday of each month

claim: The Collection de l'Art Brut, founded around Jean Dubuffet's donation, marks its 50th anniversary in February 2026 and is housed in the 18th-century Château de Beaulieu.
quote: The Collection de l'Art Brut is marking its 50th anniversary in February 2026.

claim: Lausanne Cathedral is open daily 09:00–19:00 (Apr–Sep) or 09:00–17:30 (Oct–Mar); entry to the cathedral is free, climbing the belfry tower costs CHF 6 adult / CHF 4 reduced, free for under-25s, with last tower visit 30 minutes before closing.
quote: April 1 – September 30, 2026: Monday–Sunday: 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM ... Adults (26+): 6 CHF — Children & youth (up to 25): Free ... Last tower visit: 30 minutes before closing

claim: Due to renovation of the south-transept vaults, the cathedral's rose window and its stained glass will be inaccessible until spring 2027.
quote: Due to the renovation of the vaults in the south transept, the rose and its stained glass windows will be inaccessible until spring 2027.

claim: Lausanne's Cathedral, considered the finest Gothic edifice in Switzerland, retains the nightly tradition of a watchman (le guet) calling the hours from the belfry from 22:00 to 02:00.
quote: Since 1405, a tower watchman (le guet) called the hours and this tradition continues nightly from 22:00 to 2:00.

claim: Sauvabelin Tower is a 35-metre wooden tower above Lausanne with 302 steps and 360° panoramic views over the city, Lake Geneva, the Alps and the Jura; the surrounding park has a lake, oak forests and a small animal park.
quote: The Tower of Sauvabelin requires climbing 302 steps to reach its platform ... 35 metre high ... An artificial lake...surrounded by oak forests ... Goats, woolly pigs, ducks, wild boar and various birds

claim: Sauvabelin Tower has a double-helix staircase so visitors ascend and descend on opposite sides; access is capped at 30 people for safety and the tower closes in strong wind, snow or ice.
quote: a double helix structure, with visitors ascending and descending at opposite sides ... A maximum of 30 people at same time, for security reasons.

claim: Climbing Sauvabelin Tower is free of charge, making it a no-cost panoramic viewpoint in Lausanne.
quote: Entrance is free but limited to a maximum of 50 people at a time for security reasons.
